ra: Al-Sanusi is the eponymous founder of the Sanusiyya order.
Al-Sanusi was a leading disciple of Ahmad ibn Idris before founding the Sanusiyya.
Ahmad al-Alawi is the eponymous founder of the Alawiyya order.
The Alawiyya is a branch of the Darqawi-Shadhili line, descending through the Darqawiyya.
Al-Alawi's lineage runs through the Darqawiyya founded by al-Darqawi (via al-Buzidi).
Al-Alawi taught Akbari metaphysics (wahdat al-wujud) drawn from Ibn Arabi.
Said Nursi is the founding inspiration and author whose Risale-i Nur defines the Nurcu movement.
Nursi's early formation was within the Naqshbandi-Khalidi milieu of eastern Anatolia, which shaped the Risale-i Nur.
Ahmadou Bamba is the eponymous founder of the Mouridiyya.
Bamba was first initiated in the Qadiriyya founded by Abd al-Qadir al-Jilani before establishing the Mouridiyya.
Ibrahim Niasse led the Fayda revival within the Tijaniyya.
Niasse's Fayda movement claims and develops the spiritual transmission of Ahmad al-Tijani.
The Hamalliyya is a reformist branch within the Tijaniyya.
Shaykh Hamallah claimed transmission of the Tijani way founded by Ahmad al-Tijani (the eleven-bead controversy concerns Tijani litany practice).
Muhammad al-Hafiz revitalised the Tijaniyya in Egypt.
His revival explicitly transmits the way of Ahmad al-Tijani.
Muhammad ibn al-Habib's Habibiyya is a branch of the Darqawi-Shadhili line.
His silsila descends from the Darqawiyya founded by al-Darqawi.
Inayat Khan was initiated in the Chishti order and transmitted a Chishti-rooted Sufism to the West.
His Chishti lineage traces to Mu'in al-Din Chishti, the order's founder in India.
Pir Vilayat was the son and designated successor of Hazrat Inayat Khan.
Muzaffer Ozak headed the Halveti-Jerrahi order, a branch of the Khalwatiyya.
Functional alignment: both are 20th-c. founders of universalist Sufi communities in the West; Bawa has no documented formal tariqa silsila, so this is a comparative (not lineal) link.
Nazim al-Haqqani is the eponymous head of the Naqshbandi-Haqqani order.
The Naqshbandi-Haqqani is a modern transnational branch of the Naqshbandiyya.
The Haqqani silsila descends through the Naqshbandi-Khalidi line of Khalid al-Baghdadi.
